title: Unifying topological, geometric, and complex classifications of black hole thermodynamics
summary: Black hole thermodynamics has recently witnessed three distinct classification schemes: based on local geometric properties of the temperature function, global topological invariants, and Riemann surface foliations in the complex plane. We show that these schemes can be precisely mapped onto one another in the real domain via two dictionaries: one linking thermal stability to the monotonicity of the temperature curve, and the other connecting the number of black hole states to the foliation number of a Riemann surface.
